attempts.text: The reviewed papers demonstrate advancements in machine learning by introducing MerLin, a tool bridging traditional machine learning with quantum computing and enabling end-to-end differentiable training of quantum layers. This integrated approach addresses the scalability limitations of near-term QML hardware by embedding photoonic quantum models within established ML ecosystems. The framework is tested on various datasets demonstrating its ability to assess predictive performance as well as underlying data complexity and model robustness, underscoring the utility of this integrated approach in enhancing the evaluation landscape of machine learning. This research question aims to identify the gaps that remain for theoretical understanding and practical applications in machine learning due to the gap between traditional ML and quantum computing/hybrid systems. The reviewed papers provide evidence of MerLin's applicability as a co-design tool linking algorithmic, benchmarking, and hardware capabilities to enable the advancement of machine learning by leveraging existing quantum computing systems.
